newsitem.title: FINLAND: Telecoms shares buoyed by Nokia Q3 growth.
newsitem.headline: Telecoms shares buoyed by Nokia Q3 growth.

text.p: Shares in the world's three leading mobile phone makers jumped on Thursday as Finnish Nokia Oy reported 58 percent growth in mobile phone sales and met expectations of third quarter earnings.

Nokia -- the world's second largest mobile phone producer -- reported a January-September pretax profit of 2.23 billion markka ($492.3 million), down from 3.98 billion markka in the year-ago period, but the third quarter profit showed a clear improvement over the second quarter -- 1.1 billion compared with 728 million.
The median forecast for the nine months was 2.2 billion.

Nokia shares surged 10 percent on the announcement in massive trading to set a new 254.00 markka year-high and closed in Helsinki at 249.50 markka, up 22.50 markka. Early New York trade was also strong.

Nokia propelled Swedish rival Ericsson's shares to a new life-high at 205.00 Swedish crowns -- up 12 crowns or 6.2 percent -- and as Helsinki closed, Ericsson was trading comfortably above 200 crowns in Stockholm.
Even Motorola Inc., which analysts said may suffer from Nokia's strength in mobile phones, opened up $0-1/2 at $52-1/8 on Wall Street.
Analysts were impressed by massive 58 percent year-on-year growth in third-quarter handset sales and relieved to see that Nokia had managed to put an end to earlier inventory problems.
"Nokia Mobile Phones continued to improve operating efficiency as planned, partly driven by the development towards regional focus in operations," Nokia said in its interim report.
"I am indeed very impressed," said Niklas Geust, analyst at FIM Pankkiiriliike, commenting on mobile phones sales growth.

Earlier, logistics problems dragged Nokia Mobile Phones into a first quarter loss and to only a slight second quarter profit, but Nokia now said margins were back to the levels of the third quarter of 1995 when Nokia made record profits.

"The logistics problems have now clearly been solved, at least as far as warehouse management is concerned," Geust said, pointing to a significant 1.2 billion markka overall reduction in inventories in the third quarter.
But some analysts were worried about the growth pace in telecommunications infrastructure sales.

Net sales growth of Nokia Telcommunications, the group's infrastructure arm, were weaker than expected at 26 percent year-on-year in the third quarter, and there were fears that Nokia has been the loser while Sweden's Ericsson has recently announced massive infrastructure orders.

"Infrastructure sales could be a worry. It may be that Nokia still has considerable infrastructure business to come in the fourth quarter (but) the current level of growth remains below what the company indicated at the start of the year," said Richard Kramer, analyst at Goldman Sachs in London.
Nokia acknowledged that sales had been below budget, but praised the Telecommuncations division's profits.
"Although sales of the (Telecommunications) business group grew at a somewhat slower rate than expected, profits exceeded our expectations," Nokia CEO Jorma Ollila said.
He also told analysts in a telephone conference that its 30 percent net sales growth target in telecommunications infrastructure was "aggressive", a Nokia spokesman told Reuters.
In Nokia's statement, Ollila emphasised the turnaround in handsets.
"We are especially pleased with the high growth in sales and progress in achieving operating efficiencies within Nokia Mobile Phones," Ollila said.
Nokia attributed the strong performance in mobile phones to continued buoyant demand in Europe and Asia, as well as to the recent introduction of new products.
Group net sales rose to 26.65 billion markka in January-September from 25.86 billion in the year-ago period. ($1=4.53 Markka)
